title: Cohomological description of integral adic constructible complexes
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\pi$, and residue field $k=R/(\pi)$, as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning that it has a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. On the pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ put $B=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(R/\pi^n)_X=\mathcal O_{E,X}$, with the canonical quotient $B\to k_X$ ([det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit], [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients]). Let $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proét}}\to X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. A $B$-module sheaf is constructible if it admits a finite stratification of $X$ by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification] on each of which it is pro-étale locally $B\otimes_R P$ for a finitely presented $R$-module $P$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Use the bounded constructible cohomology condition of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], and derived $(\pi)$-completeness in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete].

Here $\operatorname{Mod}(B)$ is the category of $B$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $D$ is the unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ is the small étale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and all derived tensors are relative tensors [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. For every $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B))$, the following are equivalent:

1. $K$ is bounded and every cohomology sheaf of $K$ is constructible as a $B$-module sheaf.
2. $K$ is derived $(\pi)$-complete and there exists a bounded complex $C\in D(X_{\mathrm{ét}},k)$ with constructible cohomology sheaves and finite Tor amplitude, together with an isomorphism $\nu_X^*C\simeq K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}k_X$ in $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},k_X)$.

Here finite Tor amplitude means that there are integers $a\leq b$ such that $H^i(C\otimes_{k_X}^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for every étale $k_X$-module sheaf $N$ and every $i\notin[a,b]$. Constructible étale $k_X$-module sheaves mean those which on a finite constructible locally closed stratification are locally constant with finite-dimensional $k$-values. Torsion $R$-modules $P$ are allowed; no finite dimension of $X$ or invertibility of $\ell$ on $X$ is assumed.

proof.text: The coefficient-integers DVR theorem supplies the unique maximal uniformizer ideal. Reuse the proved coefficientIntegers_complete helper of AdicLimitFiniteModules (its compact closed-ball proof of adic completeness), then transport the DVR, ideal and completeness through ULift.ringEquiv. Apply adic_stratified_perfect with these actual lifted coefficients. No ring or coefficient presentation is replaced.

The completed scalar realization is the constant-module functor followed by completed scalar extension. The former is exact by the proved constant_exact helper of CompletedConstantSheafReduction; the latter is exact by completed_constant_algebra_flat_quotients. Inverse image of modules is exact by the proved ProEtaleOperations helper, and localized module restriction is exact by localizedSystemExact. Restriction along the identity of the inverse-image coefficient ring is naturally the identity, so uniqueness of left adjoints identifies the published ringed pullback with ordinary module inverse image. Comparing both constructions on derived-category representatives identifies sfbLocalRestriction with the derived exact composite. Thus scalar realization and local restriction commute with homology and degree-zero single objects.

For each finitely presented scalar module, Module.FinitePresentation.exists_fin' gives a finite free surjection. Submodule.basisOfPid gives a finite basis of its kernel. The resulting short exact sequence has a two-term double complex in degrees -1 and 0; the existing proved twoTerm_augmentation helper identifies this complex with the module in degree zero in the derived category. Both terms are finite projective. Apply the exact scalar realization and exact local restriction to this isomorphism. Convert the finite locally closed stratification to Stratification.ofNoetherianSpace without changing any stratum or covering sieve. These are precisely the perfect models of a completed-constant stratified module in degree zero.

Apply the degreewise bounded devissage theorem already proved in DerivedCategory.TStructure. The property is IsSfbAdicConstructible; its zero, isomorphism, shift and extension closure come from adic_stratified_perfect. The previous step and the standard single-functor shift isomorphism supply every required degreewise hypothesis. This proves adic constructibility from bounded completed-constant stratified cohomology.

Conversely adic_stratified_perfect supplies boundedness and local bounded finite-projective scalar models. A scalar model has finitely generated cycles because the coefficient ring is Noetherian; its homology is a quotient of the cycles, hence finite and finitely presented. Exact scalar realization and exact local restriction identify the restricted homology of K with the restricted completed scalar realization of this homology module. Retain each original stratum and covering sieve and forget only the redundant Noetherian structure to obtain FiniteLocallyClosedStratification. These witnesses are exactly IsCompletedConstantStratified for every cohomology sheaf. This argument compares the two predicates over their common inverse-image coefficient ring and needs no new identification with coefficients constructed on the stratum.
